detections.sql:
SELECT p.sku, p.supplier_id, i.stock_count 
FROM products p 
JOIN inventory i ON p.sku = i.sku 
WHERE p.sku NOT IN (SELECT sku FROM sales_events WHERE sale_date >= date('now', '-12 months')) 
GROUP BY p.supplier_id, p.sku 
ORDER BY i.stock_count DESC 
LIMIT 3
detections.insight: The data reveals a significant inventory buildup of unsold products across two suppliers, with a combined total of 161 units. This accumulation of dead stock poses a substantial financial risk, as it ties up capital that could be better utilized elsewhere in the business. Furthermore, it may indicate inefficiencies in the supply chain, procurement, or sales processes, which need to be addressed to prevent future stockpiling. This situation also raises concerns about the potential for obsolescence, damage, or shrinkage, all of which could further exacerbate the financial impact.
detections.recommendation: To mitigate this risk, I recommend that the executive: 1. Conduct a thorough review of the procurement process to identify opportunities for improvement, focusing on more accurate demand forecasting and better supplier relationships. This could involve renegotiating contracts or exploring alternative suppliers. 2. Develop a strategic plan to liquidate the excess inventory, potentially through targeted promotions, clearance sales, or partnerships with third-party liquidators. This will help to free up capital and reduce the financial burden associated with holding onto dead stock.

narrative.executive_summary: Our platform currently faces a moderate risk of inventory-related disruptions, driven by dead stock accumulation, reorder point breaches, and supplier performance issues. These threats, while not yet critical, demand immediate attention to prevent substantial financial losses. We recommend swift action to mitigate these risks and maintain operational efficiency.

threat_vectors.name: Dead Stock Accumulation
threat_vectors.description: 161 units of unsold products across two suppliers pose a significant financial risk due to tied-up capital, potentially indicating inefficient inventory management.

threat_vectors.name: Reorder Point Breaches
threat_vectors.description: 13 instances of reorder point breaches indicate a potential disruption in inventory replenishment, requiring immediate attention to prevent stockouts or overstocking.

threat_vectors.name: Supplier Performance Issues
threat_vectors.description: Supplier delay impact analysis indicates a low-risk score of 6, but ongoing monitoring is essential to prevent potential delays or disruptions in inventory replenishment.

immediate_actions: Conduct an immediate inventory audit to identify and rectify dead stock accumulation across all suppliers.
Review and adjust reorder points to prevent future breaches, ensuring optimal inventory levels and minimizing stockouts or overstocking.
Engage with suppliers to address potential delays or performance issues, ensuring timely delivery of inventory and maintaining operational efficiency.
monitoring_recommendations: Continuously monitor inventory levels, supplier performance, and reorder points to detect potential issues before they escalate.
Implement regular supplier performance reviews to identify and address potential delays or disruptions in inventory replenishment.
Establish a centralized inventory management system to ensure real-time visibility and control over inventory levels, reducing the risk of dead stock accumulation and reorder point breaches.
